Josue De Paula voices support for Shohei Ohtani amid postseason struggles
Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula expressed confidence in Shohei Ohtani despite recent struggles at bat during the playoffs. Manager Dave Roberts also voiced support for Ohtani as both players remain key parts of Los Angeles' postseason plans.
Los Angeles Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula expressed support for teammate Shohei Ohtani during a challenging postseason, according to an exclusive interview with Dodgers Nation on Oct. 14.
De Paula, who joined the roster as a pinch hitter after making an impact late in the season, has been recognized for his strong plate approach and hitting abilities. Despite concerns about his defensive readiness, he secured one of the final roster spots over Dalton Rushing following a productive stint with the major league club while Ohtani was absent.
With Ohtani struggling at the plate and experiencing discomfort, some have suggested that De Paula should take his place in the lineup. However, De Paula said he remains confident in Ohtani's abilities: “I mean, I have no fear. Sho is a hell of a player. Amazing player. So, I feel like he’s going to bounce back. I mean, this is baseball. Stuff happens,” De Paula said to Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
He continued: “Obviously, it can happen to any player. And I feel like in any moment, we’re going to see something crazy from Sho. So, all I’ve got to say to the fans is never sleep on him.”
Ohtani has gone 3-for-24 in the postseason so far with three walks and seven strikeouts; his performance has declined further in the National League Championship Series where he is 1-for-7 with a walk. Despite these numbers, manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Ohtani remains in Wednesday's lineup, and said that Ohtani feels confident about contributing during the playoffs.
“He expects a lot from himself, and he hasn’t performed to his expectations… this was a different look from Shohei yesterday, and that’s an understatement,” Roberts said.
The Dodgers organization continues to rely on Ohtani's ability to make adjustments as they pursue success in the postseason.
